# Current production preimages — fixture source only

These overlays compose the September 17 installed Alerts authority with Union37. The newly composed full37 path is **UNRUN**; these fixture files are not production migrations and do not establish Union installation or delivery. The original full-schema capture, correction captures, bootstrap files and standalone Alerts tests remain unchanged.

Load these files once per fresh full-schema cluster, **after every retained catalog/dependency bootstrap and before any legacy financial producer, negative-fixture mutation, or candidate component**:

1. `alerts-and-ledger.sql` requires the exact original bridge/raiser definitions and ACLs, replaces only those fixture definitions with the exact accepted current images, and creates the actual additional ledger index.
2. `owner-notification-coexistence.sql` supplies only the actual dependency closure needed by the current owner routing predicate and BEFORE capture: four functions, the two inbox/destination tables, their indexes/constraints/ACLs and identity sequence, plus the two current notification triggers. It preserves the existing deferred accounting constraint trigger and mirror function.
3. `direct-intake-prerequisites.sql` restores the exact missing engine-alert tables/recorder, captured sequence access and missing secondary indexes from the separately qualified Alerts fixture. Its local allocation guard is adapted to this existing PostgreSQL17/socket/owner fixture, and it refuses unexpected objects or a used/changed retained sequence. No sequence is reset. The generic operational recorder and owner-notification core must already exist.
4. `direct-intake-installed.sql` is the byte-identical 54,826-byte packet installed as `20260917062322` (SHA256 `7f7020ee71fe1bd6475dff8de572cd96e7cac888c3923245f7fbc54e8ff161dd`). It retains its original transaction, locks, full incoming catalog equality and exact postconditions. The three `a00_operational_source_intake` AFTER INSERT/UPDATE hooks capture the real engine/financial/incident source rows into two private tables. Its earlier SOURCE ONLY comment is preserved as historical bytes; the later receipt establishes the actual Alerts installation, not Union qualification.

The parent owns runner registration and source-binding updates. This directory must not enter the production activation bundle. Component34 now demands the exact installed bridge hash; component36 demands the exact installed 21-argument raiser hash and ledger-index inventory. No old/new hash alternatives were added and neither Alerts business function is replaced by Union37.

## Actual provenance

`captured-authority.json` retains metadata-only results and exact query path/hash provenance from project `kuklfnapbkmacvwxktbh`. Every successful capture ran inside REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY with 10-second statement and 2-second lock timeouts, ending in ROLLBACK. No production user rows or business functions were read/invoked. Parent outputs retain raw tool responses and queries under `outputs/union-provider-preflight-20260917`. The sequence maximum is explicitly captured as text in capture16 because numeric JSON transport lost precision in capture15.

The two Alerts definitions match byte for byte the accepted `post` images of installed migration `20260917024440`, maintained in `supabase/components/production-alert-identity-and-rake-wording.sql` (SHA256 `6622531f15dc53dc532dcba4d7441f5907be06be62decca528baf8d94a235710`). The bridge preserves exact failed-leave table/hand identity and handles malformed table IDs safely. The raiser preserves the corrected detector-storm explanation. The later rake-wording escalator is neither changed nor required by these two overlays.

The ledger index is exactly `idx_chip_ledger_tournament_category`, a nonunique B-tree on `(tournament_id, category)` where tournament_id is nonnull. This is current metadata, not a new financial rule.

## Historical fixture omissions

The original schema already creates `operational_alert_events_id_seq` but omits its inbox table, identity dependency, recorder function and owner destination closure. The owner overlay refuses anything except that unused, unattached, owner-only PostgreSQL17 fixture sequence with the exact original sequence parameters. It removes that known orphan with RESTRICT and recreates the real identity-owned sequence as part of the captured table. It refuses preexisting tables, indexes and function names, and verifies the complete two-table shape, exact function definitions/access, sequence dependency/access and notification triggers before commit. This is isolated fixture restoration; no production sequence is dropped or adopted.

The original schema's generic notification trigger is unconditional. Current production instead has `WHEN NOT fn_is_owner_operational_notification(...)` plus `zz_capture_owner_notification_destination BEFORE INSERT`. The captured predicate excludes both accounting invoice types; the BEFORE function returns NEW unchanged. The existing mirror's TG_NAME branch defers accounting invoices until the genuine delivery link exists. These source facts do not replace a native producer/delivery/replay test.

## Qualification limits

The overlays do not add the personal feed view, administrative reader/retry routes, background jobs or any financial producer stub. They include the exact recorder dependency actually called by the BEFORE trigger, so a producer can exercise both preserved Alerts capture and genuine accounting delivery in the full-schema fixture. Native execution, failure rollback, owner and ordinary-recipient genuine invoice cases, authenticated APIs and provider/device delivery remain separate required evidence. Existing native suites must run against these overlays; source preparation is not a passing test result.

## Direct intake provenance and capture coverage

`direct-intake-authority.raw.txt` preserves the owner's exact catalog capture, complete old recorder definition and sequence/role supplements. `direct-intake-installation-receipt.raw.txt` preserves the later installed readback receipt: owner HEAD `4008d2020f95d411953f77f1fe07bdc2fed6d94c`, required native run `35189029570`, job `105097355508`, and independent readback at `2026-09-17T06:23:35.198329+00:00`. It establishes exact helper/private-relation/hook installation with engine recorder MD5 `3b97b07170b81947137ee2adfc268717`; natural event delivery remains pending in that receipt. This is the last successful equivalent Alerts qualification, not a successful full37 run.

`direct-intake-provenance.json` records byte hashes, exact source paths, permitted fixture-only transformations and the load order. The raw files use `.raw.txt` to preserve the captured bytes through ordinary JSON formatting hooks. The old original fixture captures are not rewritten.

The existing whole-cluster rollback state now includes `operational_source_intake` alongside all previous schemas. Accepted-authority capture includes its helper/namespace/table/column permissions, constraints, indexes, policies and triggers, plus the real source tables. Correction and credit full-state helpers include the private snapshot/delivery rows; correction's enumerated snapshot also covers the shared operational inbox and owner-notification destination. Sequences remain outside transactional row equality because allocation gaps do not roll back. Original immutable correction/credit assertions and financial stores remain unchanged.

The installed packet's guards qualify the fixture overlay, not the live Union candidate. Components34/36 must accept the exact new incident hook in their existing trigger inventories. A live install preflight must also pin the actual direct hook/helper function bodies, owners/configuration/ACLs and private table authority against the retained installed readback; a matching function name alone is not body provenance. No Alerts business logic, financial writer, notification mirror, dispatcher, historical source row or automatic task activation is introduced by this fixture composition.

## Installed finish-lane successor composition

`finish-lane-prerequisites.sql` restores only the two exact captured function omissions required by installed PR4761: the table shared-lane helper and committed seat-move resolver. It requires the original isolated PostgreSQL17 fixture, absent target function names and the exact old global helper, then proves full definitions, body hashes, owner/configuration and raw/effective grants. The existing runner then applies the maintained `20260917113717_the_finish_lane_is_exclusive_among_finishes.sql` byte for byte, preserving all of its guards and its transaction. `finish-lane-installed-readback.sql` checks all four successor definitions and their authority against the separately retained installed capture before Union37. No Union component or historical capture changes.

`finish-lane-successor-provenance.json` binds the migration, three exact raw metadata captures and both fixture SQL files. The seat-move resolver is a catalog dependency of the migration's exact global-lane inventory; its separate receipt reader is absent from this historical fixture, and seat movement is not exercised or qualified here. No unrelated production catalog is reconstructed.

The existing normal lifecycle case checks G shared, F exclusive and its own T exclusive after real nested Union settlement, with no G/B exclusive upgrade. The existing late terminal fault also proves exact lock/transaction-local-setting rollback, and successful replay plus the outcome resolver must retain the same narrow lane. These silent lock checks preserve the existing PASS count and all financial assertions. The earning case retains its existing positive commission/fee rollback and replay checks; an earlier satellite in that transaction already owns G/B exclusively, so it is not a narrower-lock witness. No new phase or concurrency harness is introduced.

The last equivalent full Union run was `35219096812`, successful on `038086f91cd0b78e96dc4aee324c25d20fc97fed`; it predates this composition. The new composed path remains **UNRUN** until the existing required native check. Source review does not certify installation, production concurrency or delivery.
